text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- In 1993, Portugal had the highest number of families in the European Union -- 2.5 million people -- living below the poverty line, a report from the European Commission says.
- Macau businessman Stanley Ho announced plans to create a new trust to receive revenues from casinos, substituting the Oriente Foundation.
- The construction companies' association forecasts growth of seven pct for the building sector in 1997. Employment in the sector rose by 13.5 percent year-on-year in the first quarter of 1997.
- The Employment Ministry has created a new institute for training and innovation, which will take over responsibility from another body for managing resources provided by the European Social Fund.

- Siemens started building a 10 billion escudo factory to manufacture electrical condensers in Evora in southern Portugal. The factory will begin operations in 1998, creating 700 jobs in the first three years.

- Five textile companies in central Portugal were the first to be chosen to benefit from the Economy Ministry's plan to restructure ailing companies. The decision was made taken because of a lack of job opportunities in the region.
- According to a bill before parliament, the government will authorise private sector companies to operate in areas such as telecomunications, mail and the arms industry.

- An accident on a bridge being built across the River Tagus on April 10, in which six people were killed, was caused by a lack of security measures, according to a commission which investigated the incident.
